measured.contract: keeps the contract the mod's stock players share: their animations at their numbers, their shared bones, attachments and bodyparts

M1.reason: Measured overlap is 0.82 to 0.84 in every view, so the outlines pass the 0.80 line. The side views still differ at the feet: in left/right (the reproduction's boots in those views) the boots are squared-off blocks with flat bottoms, where the original's taper to a point. The below view shows a square notch at the upper right that the original lacks. Those outline differences are real, not paint, so M1 is 1.

M2.reason: Measured size: length 25.3 vs 23.7 (6.9% off), width 22.2 vs 22.0 (0.8%), height 69.2 vs 69.4 (0.4%). All within 10%.

M3.reason: The original's boots have laces and eyelets on the front and sides (visible in the front and front-left views), and the reproduction's boots read as plain dark shapes without them. The boot shape itself is wrong: blocks with flat soles in the left and right views, not the original's tapered boots. The row of gold studs on the chest (front view) is faint in the reproduction. Small parts missing and a wrong boot form cap M3 at 1. Vest, mask, gloves, pants pockets and knee pads are present.

M4.reason: Measured colour difference is 3.1 mean delta E, with 2.3 to 3.7 in every view and shared outline 0.79 to 0.84. Black vest, black mask and boots, grey-white camo trousers and skin with tattoos match the original's regions in all views.

M5.reason: The SIX lettering on the back and the forearm tattoos are present, but softer and less sharp than the original's (visible at the back and front-right views). The camo on the trousers has less contrast and less wear, and the chest studs are blurred. Not a must-have item.

M6.reason: Side by side at game size it reads as the same character, but a player comparing the two would notice the blockier boots and the squared-off feet in the side views (left and right), and the softer markings. Judged on the side-by-side only, not the line-up.

M7.reason: The front is the original's front, the figure stands upright with both feet on the ground in the front and back views, and it stands on its origin as the original does.

M8.reason: The SMAK check reports no errors. Triangles are 1296 against the original's 873 (1.48 times, under 2 times). No open, inside-out or floating parts are visible in any view.

C1.reason: Run (30 frames), attack (20 frames) and forward dive (35 frames) all play with the parts on the body. The arms, legs and boots move with the torso in each frame, and nothing comes apart, sinks or floats.

C2.reason: The contract is reported as kept, and checkErrors is empty. The run, attack and dive all play at their numbers, which indicates the bones and animations are in place. I cannot confirm bone-by-bone attachments from the pictures, so this rests on the reported contract and the playback.
